content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a cucumber cream cheese sandwich, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Slice the cucumber into thin rounds (2 minutes)
Step 2. Retrieve a clean butter knife from the drawer (10 seconds)
Step 3. Soften the cream cheese in a small bowl (5 minutes)
Step 4. Toast the bread slices to a golden brown (3 minutes)
Step 5. Lightly butter the outside of the bread (45 seconds)
Step 6. Wash the fresh dill under cold water (30 seconds)
Step 7. Peel the skin off the cucumber (1 minute)
Step 8. Take the bread loaf out of the pantry (20 seconds)
Step 9. Locate the bunch of dill in the refrigerator (15 seconds)
Step 10. Clear a space on the counter for assembly (1 minute)
Step 11. Find the salt and pepper shakers (30 seconds)
Step 12. Pat the dill dry with a paper towel (20 seconds)
Step 13. Pick the freshest sprigs of dill (40 seconds)
Step 14. Chop the dill finely (1 minute)
Step 15. Mix the herbs into the cream cheese (2 minutes)
Step 16. Remove the thick stems from the dill (45 seconds)
Step 17. Mince a small clove of garlic (2 minutes)
Step 18. Sprinkle salt and pepper over the sandwich filling (15 seconds)
Step 19. Grind fresh black pepper (20 seconds)
Step 20. Spread the garlic-herb mixture onto the bread (1 minute)
Step 21. Slice the ends off the cucumber (30 seconds)
Step 22. Measure out two tablespoons of cream cheese (30 seconds)
Step 23. Spread a layer of plain cream cheese as a moisture barrier (45 seconds)
Step 24. Set out a serving plate (15 seconds)
Step 25. Season the cucumber slices individually (1 minute)
Step 26. Open the cream cheese container (10 seconds)
Step 27. Rinse the peeled cucumber (20 seconds)
Step 28. Gather the cutting board and chef's knife (30 seconds)
Step 29. Combine the minced garlic with the cream cheese (1 minute)
Step 30. Get the butter dish from the fridge (15 seconds)
Step 31. Check the cucumber for bitterness (10 seconds)
Step 32. Take the cream cheese out to reach room temperature (30 minutes)
Step 33. Place the cucumber slices on a paper towel to drain (5 minutes)
Step 34. Remove two slices of bread (15 seconds)
Step 35. Wipe the knife clean (15 seconds)
Step 36. Zest a small amount of lemon (1 minute)
Step 37. Clean the kitchen island surface (3 minutes)
Step 38. Move the toaster to a convenient outlet (20 seconds)
Step 39. Compost the dill stems and cucumber ends (40 seconds)
Step 40. Wash the cutting board (2 minutes)
